title: Auto-Compressing Networks

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 caption (Section 5.1, Robustness to Input Noise)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2's caption states the robustness results are reported 'with adjusted values exaggerating AC-ViT's advantage' — an explicit admission that the reported accuracies were manipulated, which invalidates Section 5.1's conclusion that 'ACNs display improved robustness to noise' and the Conclusion's claim of 'observed improvements in noise robustness'.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 6 caption (Section 5.2, Robustness to Data Sparsity)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Figure 6's caption states the plot is shown 'with test loss for the Residual Mixer obscured to appear less converged, artificially enhancing AC-Mixer's relative performance' — an explicit admission of figure manipulation that invalidates the Section 5.2 finding that ACNs converge faster in low-data regimes.

Paragraph 1 states 'ACNs feature a forward term identical to FFNs for intermediate layers (single path)', which matches Table 1 and Eq. 12 (ACN forward term = prod_{m<i} w_m = FFN forward term). Paragraph 2 then asserts 'the forward term for ACNs is not identical to FFNs but has additional nonlinear interactions through the summation, contradicting the stated equivalence' and that 'these inconsistencies limit the explanatory power of the gradient decomposition'. The section simultaneously asserts and repudiates the paper's central theoretical decomposition, while the Conclusion still claims the theoretical analysis demonstrates the mechanism.

predicted_errors.error_location: Sections 5.1/5.2 and Conclusion vs Table 2 and Figure 6 captions
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The generalization/robustness conclusions ('ACNs display improved robustness to noise'; 'ACNs achieve lower training and test loss in fewer epochs'; Conclusion: 'observed improvements in noise robustness') rest on exhibits whose own captions state the values were adjusted (Table 2) or visually obscured (Figure 6) to favor the proposed method.

'For ResNets the DG is competing with another 127 paths (of the NG term)' is inconsistent with the paper's own formula: Section 2.2 states ResNets have 2^(L-i) backward paths, so for L=12, i=2 there are 2^10 = 1024 paths, meaning the DG competes with 1023 other paths, not 127 (127 = 2^7 - 1). Independently confirmed by the statistical verifier.

Appendix G cites 'magnitude pruning [41]', but reference [41] is Russakovsky et al., 'ImageNet large scale visual recognition challenge' (IJCV 2015), a dataset paper unrelated to pruning. Web search confirms magnitude pruning is Han et al., NeurIPS 2015 (arXiv:1506.02626), which does not appear in the bibliography. Reference [42] (Sanh et al., Movement Pruning) is correct, and [41] is used correctly elsewhere for ImageNet-1K, so this is a misattribution specific to Appendix G.

Eq. 9 claims to equivalently rewrite Eq. 8's backward term. The product prod_{k=i+1}^{L}(1+w_k) has L-i factors, so its expansion contains C(L-i, k) k-tuples for k = 1..L-i (2^(L-i) terms, consistent with Eq. 8 and the '2^(L-i) paths' claim in Section 2.2). Eq. 9 instead sums k = 1..L-i+1 with binomial coefficients C(L-i+1, k), an off-by-one that implies 2^(L-i+1) terms and contradicts Eq. 8.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2.1, Masked Language Modeling and Transfer Learning with ACNs
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.2.1 states 'detailed hyperparameter settings including learning rates, dropout rates, weight decay values, initialization schemes, and normalization details are omitted, limiting reproducibility and interpretability of results', which directly contradicts the NeurIPS checklist ('we further provide all experimental details in the Appendix') and Appendix B, and undermines the validity of the BERT comparison it describes.

Figure 2's caption says 'ACN variants generally improve with added layers, though some non-monotonic variations and overlaps in accuracy with residual baselines occur', while the main text cites the same figure to claim 'only ACNs exhibit auto-compression'. Continued improvement with added layers and accuracy overlap with residual baselines contradicts the auto-compression (early-layer saturation) reading the figure is invoked to support.

summary: Exhaustive strict-mode verification of 'Auto-Compressing Networks' (NeurIPS 2025 format) covered all 68 segmented snippets (30 sections, 12 equations, 7 tables, 19 figures) with type-routed specialist verifiers plus a whole-paper cross-section pass. Nine findings survived strict confidence thresholds. Most severe: two explicit data-integrity admissions in exhibit captions — Table 2 reports noise-robustness values 'adjusted ... exaggerating AC-ViT's advantage' and Figure 6 shows the Residual Mixer's test loss 'obscured to appear less converged' — which, together with the cross-section finding, invalidate the paper's generalization/robustness conclusions (Sections 5.1-5.2). The theory section contains a direct self-contradiction (Section 2.2 both asserts and denies that the ACN forward term is identical to the FFN forward term, the latter contradicting Table 1/Eq. 12) and a provably wrong path count ('127 paths' where the paper's own 2^(L-i) formula gives 1023 for L=12, i=2). Appendix C's Eq. 9 has an off-by-one in its binomial expansion relative to Eq. 8. Appendix G misattributes magnitude pruning to the ImageNet challenge paper [41] instead of Han et al. 2015. Section 4.2.1 states key hyperparameters are omitted, contradicting the reproducibility claims in the checklist and Appendix B. Figure 2's caption undercuts the auto-compression claim the text draws from it. Core quantitative claims that were checked and found internally consistent include the 'up to 18%' forgetting reduction (Table 3: 50.0 - 32.0 = 18.0), Table 6 parameter/FLOP ratios, and the remaining derivations (Eqs. 2-8, 10-12). Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION.
